name: Introduction to Python
description: What Python is, how programs are run, basic syntax rules, and how to read error messages.

subconcepts.name: What Python is and how code is executed (interpreter)
Running code: interactive shell vs script file

common_misconceptions.description: Inconsistent or missing indentation, or indenting a statement that should not be indented.
Assuming Python is case-insensitive (e.g. Print vs print, Name vs name).
Expecting values to be displayed automatically in a script the way they are in the interactive shell.
Not reading the error message or line number and guessing at fixes.

name: Variables and Data Types
description: Naming and assigning variables, the core built-in types, and converting between them.

subconcepts.name: Core types: int, float, str, bool
Reassignment and variable lifetime within a program

common_misconceptions.description: Reading x = 5 as a mathematical equality rather than storing a value; confusion over x = x + 1.
Using names with spaces, leading digits, or reserved keywords.
Treating "5" and 5 as the same value or type.
Concatenating a string with a number without conversion, causing TypeError.
Using a variable before it has been assigned, causing NameError.

name: Input and Output
description: Displaying output with print and f-strings, and reading user input.

subconcepts.name: Reading multiple values from one line

common_misconceptions.description: Expecting input() to return a number, so arithmetic on it fails or concatenates.
Missing parentheses or mismatched quotes in print calls.
Forgetting the f prefix so {variable} is printed literally.
Believing print() stores or changes a value rather than only displaying it.
Using values from split() as numbers without converting them.

name: Operators
description: Arithmetic, comparison, logical, assignment, and membership operators, plus precedence.

common_misconceptions.description: Confusing / (float result) with // (floor division).
Using = where == is needed, or the reverse.
Assuming left-to-right evaluation without regard to precedence.
Using is to compare values instead of ==.
Writing x == 1 or 2 expecting it to test both values.
Not understanding % as a remainder, e.g. in even/odd or wrap-around checks.

name: Conditional Statements (if, elif, else)
description: Branching program flow with if, elif, and else based on boolean conditions.

common_misconceptions.description: Omitting the colon after if, elif, or else.
Using = instead of == inside a condition.
Using separate if statements where mutually exclusive elif branches are needed.
Ordering elif branches so a broader condition shadows a narrower one.
Misplacing indentation so statements fall inside or outside the intended branch.
Misjudging which values (0, empty string, empty list, None) count as False.

name: Loops (for, while)
description: Repeating code with for and while loops, loop control, and common loop patterns.

common_misconceptions.description: Misjudging range() bounds, since the stop value is exclusive.
Writing a while loop whose condition variable is never updated.
Adding or removing items from a list while looping over it.
Initialising the accumulator or counter inside the loop body.
Confusing break (exit loop) with continue (skip to next iteration).
Misunderstanding the loop variable, e.g. expecting it to be an index when iterating over values.

name: Strings
description: Indexing, slicing, immutability, and common methods for working with text.

subconcepts.name: Common methods (upper, lower, strip, split, join, replace, find)
Searching and iterating over strings (in, count, loops)

common_misconceptions.description: Trying to assign to a character, e.g. s[0] = 'x'.
Indexing past the end of a string, or mixing up 0-based and 1-based positions.
Forgetting that the slice end index is excluded.
Calling s.upper() or s.strip() without saving the returned new string.
Comparing strings without accounting for letter case.
Mixing up split() (string to list) and join() (list to string), or the join separator syntax.

name: Lists, Tuples, and Sets
description: Ordered mutable lists, immutable tuples, and unordered unique sets.

subconcepts.name: List methods (append, extend, insert, remove, pop, sort)
Membership, len(), and iteration over collections

common_misconceptions.description: Assuming b = a copies a list, when both names refer to the same list.
Writing x = lst.sort() and expecting a sorted list back.
Confusing append (adds one item) with extend (adds each item of an iterable).
Trying to modify a tuple in place.
Forgetting the trailing comma in a one-element tuple.
Indexing a set or assuming it keeps insertion order.
Accessing an index that does not exist, including off-by-one on len().
Confusing remove (by value) with pop (by index).

name: Dictionaries
description: Key-value mappings: creating, accessing, updating, and iterating.

subconcepts.name: Iterating over keys, values, and items

common_misconceptions.description: Accessing a key that may not exist with [] instead of get() or an in check.
Using a list or other mutable type as a dictionary key.
Expecting a for loop over a dictionary to yield values or pairs rather than keys.
Adding or deleting keys while looping over the dictionary.
Mixing up keys and values when looking up or inverting entries.
Not realising a repeated key silently overwrites the earlier value.

name: Functions
description: Defining reusable functions: parameters, return values, defaults, and scope.

common_misconceptions.description: Using print() inside a function when the caller needs a returned value.
Forgetting return, so the call evaluates to None.
Defining a function but never calling it.
Trying to use a function's local variable outside the function.
Using a mutable default such as [] that persists between calls.
Passing the wrong number or order of arguments.
Placing return inside a loop so it exits on the first iteration.

name: List Comprehensions
description: Building lists concisely from iterables, with optional filtering and transformation.

common_misconceptions.description: Putting the if filter and the if-else expression in the wrong position.
Reversing the order of the for clauses in a nested comprehension.
Using a comprehension for side effects such as printing instead of building a list.
Cramming too much logic into one comprehension where a loop would be clearer.
Using () or {} and getting a generator or set instead of a list.

name: Exception Handling
description: Handling runtime errors with try/except and raising exceptions deliberately.

subconcepts.name: Common exception types and reading tracebacks

common_misconceptions.description: Using a bare except: that hides the actual error type.
Catching an exception and doing nothing, so failures go unnoticed.
Wrapping far more code than necessary in a single try block.
Confusing when else (no exception) and finally (always) run.
Expecting try/except to catch syntax errors.
Catching an exception type that the code does not actually raise.

name: File Handling
description: Reading from and writing to text files safely.

subconcepts.name: Opening and closing files; file modes
Processing file contents line by line

common_misconceptions.description: Not closing a file or not using with, risking unflushed data or leaked handles.
Opening with 'w' and unintentionally erasing existing content instead of using 'a'.
Forgetting that lines read from a file keep the trailing newline.
Reading a file twice without reopening it or seeking, getting empty results.
Using a path that is relative to a different working directory.
Expecting read() to return a list of lines or numbers rather than one string.
